source: Derm Expert, originally published in Essential Evidence Plus by Wiley (archived 2026-11-25).

morphologies.name: Atrophy
morphologies.description: Loss of skin substance (can be epidermal, dermal, subcutaneous)

morphologies.name: Blisters, vesicles, and bullae
morphologies.description: Circumscribed, thin-walled elevated lesion containing fluid

morphologies.name: Erosions and excoriations
morphologies.description: Circumscribed lesions lacking the upper layer of skin

morphologies.name: Hair and scalp
morphologies.description: Lesions of the hair and scalp

children.name: Acquired hair loss with normal scalp appearance
Hair loss with scarring of scalp

morphologies.name: Macules and patches
morphologies.description: Flat, circumscribed area with change in skin color

morphologies.name: Mouth, lip and tongue
morphologies.description: Lesions of the mouth, lips, and tongue

morphologies.name: Nails
morphologies.description: Lesions of the nails and nail bed

morphologies.name: Nodules
morphologies.description: Solid, palpable lesion in dermis or subcutaneous (deeper than papule)

children.name: Flesh-colored to red, sparse, nontender nodules

morphologies.name: Papules and plaques
morphologies.description: Solid lesion (typically dome-shaped) usually elevated above surrounding skin

children.name: Multiple papules which tend to be symmetrical

morphologies.name: Purpura
morphologies.description: Non-blanching red/purple lesion resulting from hemorrhage into skin

children.name: Pustules confined to palms and soles
Sparse, primarily acral pustules with hemorrhage

morphologies.name: Ulcers
morphologies.description: Depressed lesions lacking epidermis and at least part of dermis
